triage.reason: At -30 °C the motor stopped 13 ms after the pinch force passed 100 N, against a 10 ms limit. A pinch is not stopped in time, which is a safety miss.

Window stops working about 50 s after ignition off, against a 60 s retained-power spec. A limit is missed with no safety effect. The reporter asks whether the spec is 60 s; confirm against the requirement.
WLC_Status period is 97 to 104 ms, within 100 ms ±10 ms. Information only, no failure.

At about -20 °C an express close reversed at about 150 mm with nothing in the window. This is a false reversal in normal use, intermittent, and it worked on retry. Earliest report of the cold false-reversal problem.
Comment typo above the DTC table (B1A10 should be B1A01). The code is correct. Documentation only.
Same late pinch stop at -30 °C (14 ms against a 10 ms limit). The low-supply condition does not change the symptom. DR-1001 is the earlier report of this problem.
Sleep current is 140 µA against a 100 µA limit. The CAN transceiver stays in standby instead of sleep. A limit is missed with no safety effect.

While closing on cobblestones the window reversed by itself, 2 of 10 tries. This is a false reversal in normal use. Its cause is road-induced, so it is not a duplicate of the cold-weather reversals (DR-1004).
A 27 A overcurrent for 100 ms stopped the motor, but B1A02 was not stored and the fault state stayed 0. The fault is not recorded, so a diagnostic function is lost. Earliest report of this problem.

Too vague to judge. Two clinic drivers said the window reacts late, but there is no measurement, no latency value, and no spec. Severity is provisional; a switch-to-motor-command timing measurement is needed.
Auto-up reversed at -18 °C with no obstacle present. Same cold false-reversal problem as DR-1004, which is earlier.
After the model passed 140 °C, one open request still moved the window. The thermal block lets one opening through. Earliest report of this problem.
After 200 cycles the reported position at the top seal is 3.5 mm instead of 0 mm. This is a position accuracy failure that grows with use and could affect normalization-dependent functions.
Motor command stays on 180 ms after switch release at 16 V, against a 100 ms limit. At 13.5 V it is 60 ms, so the overrun depends on voltage. A limit is missed with no safety effect identified.
Retained power is about 45 s against a 60 s spec. Same retained-power shortfall as DR-1002, which is earlier.

One WLC_Status frame was missing during 100 diagnostic requests, with a 200 ms gap instead of 100 ms. Intermittent timing violation under diagnostic load. Differs from DR-1003 (jitter within limit) and DR-1022 (response latency); a shared load cause should be checked.
Draft owner's manual page 14 shows the switch symbol upside down. Documentation fix only; no design change.

With the Hall signal disconnected while closing at 9 V, the motor ran 1.2 s to the end stop and no DTC was stored. Motor runs without position feedback. If pinch detection relies on Hall feedback, anti-pinch is bypassed. Needs confirmation of the pinch dependency.
At an estimated 143 °C the window opened once, the same thermal block failure as DR-1012. The reporter asks if it was seen before; DR-1012 is the earlier matching report in this batch.

After battery disconnect (not normalized), a short press up closed the window fully. Express close should be blocked until normalized. Escalate to S1 if anti-pinch is not active during un-normalized express close; that is not stated in the report.
Unused variable t_prev in thermal_model.c causes a compiler warning. No behaviour impact.
3 of 100 diagnostic responses took 55 to 62 ms against a 50 ms limit, during motor start. Rare timing miss with no safety effect. Differs from DR-1016 (missing frame).
Unintended reversal while closing over cobblestones, nothing trapped. Same road-induced false reversal as DR-1008, which is earlier.
Applying -14 V for 60 s left the controller unable to wake, with protection diode D3 open. Controller function is lost and reverse-polarity protection failed.
Undervoltage stop after 21 ms at 5.5 V, within the 50 ms limit. Information only.
Clinic drivers hear a loud knock when the window reaches the top. No damage seen. Degraded comfort and end-stop behaviour in normal use; no numeric spec cited, so severity is provisional.
Hall connector pulled during auto-up: window ran into the seal and kept pushing, and no DTC was stored. Same Hall-loss problem as DR-1018, which is earlier.
Inrush current of 14 A for 40 ms at 16 V. No spec limit, so not a failure. Information and a proposed requirement only.
After overcurrent the motor stops, but the fault state stays 0 and fault memory is empty (TC-DG-02). Same problem as DR-1009, which is earlier.
At 85 °C the pinch reversal distance was 146 mm against a 150 mm limit. This is a safety reversal distance miss. Not a duplicate of DR-1001 (different metric and temperature).
